newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge to question Algerian rebel in USA.
newsitem.headline: French judge to question Algerian rebel in USA.

text.p: A French investigating magistrate is visiting the United States to question a detained Algerian suspected of being involved in a Moslem fundamentalist rebel network, French judicial sources said on Tuesday.
They said magistrate Roger Le Loire, who flew to the United States on Monday, was likely to formally place the detainee, Anwar Haddam, under investigation on suspicion of conspiring to terrorism.

Haddam, a leading member of Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), is being held in Manassas, Virginia. He staged a hunger strike in jail last May ito press his case for political asylum or a chance to seek refuge abroad.
He was detained on December 6 after the visa that had let him stay legally in the United States while awaiting a ruling on his asylum request had expired.

The judicial sources said he was suspected of being involved in providing forged documents to FIS members and circulating FIS propaganda. They said the case was not related to a series of bloody bombings in France in 1995 that have been blamed on Algerian rebels.
Haddam, who served as FIS spokesman in the United States, was among 188 Islamic militants who won seats in Algeria's 430-member legislature in the first round of an election in December 1991.
The Algerian government cancelled a runoff in January 1992, depriving the FIS of a likely victory. Civil strife in the North African country has since claimed an estimated 60,000 lives.
